summary.text: Amy Huffman Oliver is the Democratic candidate for Indiana House of Representatives District 62 in the November 3, 2026 general election. An attorney and former prosecutor, she says she has served six years on the Brown County School Board and taught history for six years.

paragraphs.text: Amy Huffman Oliver was born in Bloomington, Indiana, graduated from Columbus North High School, and earned a bachelor's degree from Smith College in 1989 and a law degree from the Indiana University School of Law in 1992.

In a Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as a fourth-generation Hoosier and native of Brown County who began her law career in Indianapolis with her husband before returning to Brown County to raise their two sons.

Oliver said she has more than 20 years of legal experience as a public service attorney and prosecutor, including work with people facing domestic violence, addiction and homelessness, along with six years as a history teacher and six years as an elected member of the Brown County School Board.
She advanced from the Democratic primary on May 5, 2026.

She said she would support additional funding for child care, rural hospitals, roads and bridges, and emergency services, and that she wants to see more affordable housing, broadband expansion and jobs that pay a living wage.
